video.title: Don't Build Anything Until You Do This | Digital Product Validation

summary: Dark Horse Entrepreneur host explains a weekend plan to validate a small digital product (ebook, template pack, prompt library, mini course) before building it. Evidence must cost the buyer something: existing spend, specific pain in their own words, or commitment (email, call, pre-order, payment). The plan sets go/fix/kill thresholds on Friday, researches buyers on Saturday, then writes a one-paragraph offer, builds a mock-up and landing page, and asks for a real commitment on Sunday. Key takeaway: opinions are worthless, pre-sales are the strongest evidence, and a killed idea is a cheap win.

ideas.name: Pre-validated micro digital product (e.g. Month-End Receipt Rescue Kit for solo bookkeepers)
ideas.one_liner: Validate a niche low-priced digital product with a weekend pre-sale before building it.
ideas.business_model: One-off sales of small digital products (checklists, email templates, kits), pre-sold before creation
ideas.customer: A narrowly defined buyer, e.g. solo bookkeepers who lose two hours each month end chasing client receipts
ideas.problem: Creators build digital products fast with ChatGPT but without proof of demand, leading to no sales.

pricing.model: Low one-off price; avoid free because price tests demand
pricing.notes: Host says first small products usually start low; thresholds should be adjusted to audience size and price.

acquisition_channels.details: Message 10-20 people matching the buyer persona in communities (Reddit, Facebook groups, niche forums) where pain was found; lead with a question, respect group no-promo rules.

quote.text: Message 10 to 20 people who fit your buyer description.

acquisition_channels.details: Share landing page in profiles and any small existing audience.
Research existing spend on Gumroad, Etsy, Teachable, Stan Store, Amazon books to see reviews and sales counts.

ideas.delivery: Digital files delivered by the creator after a pre-sale on a stated ship date; the product is built only after the go signal, using collected customer quotes as the outline. Full refund offered if not built.
unit_economics_claims: Host ran a pre-sale for a not-yet-created podcasting course and got 18 sign-ups in two hours
Go threshold: at least 3 non-acquaintances commit, ideally paying
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated precisely; a weekend of time plus a landing page and payment option
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Pre-sale evidence within one weekend (48 hours)

acquisition.how: Research and quote grouping can be agent-assisted, but community outreach and conversations are manual and cold DMs to individuals face PECR limits; inbound listings and SEO are more automatable.

onboarding.how: Landing page, payment and automated delivery email are standard software.

delivery.how: Digital files can be drafted by AI with human review and delivered automatically.

billing.how: Payment platforms handle checkout, refunds and receipts.

support.how: Low-touch product; an agent can answer FAQs with occasional human refunds or edge cases.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; digital products sell globally. Pre-sales need clear delivery dates and refunds under UK consumer law, and VAT on digital sales applies. Avoid cold DMs to individuals under PECR; ask questions in communities where allowed.

risks: Small numbers are noisy; 3 buyers does not mean 300
Crowded markets for generic templates and prompt packs
Fake AI reviews or testimonials are unethical and risky

tactics.name: Set go/fix/kill thresholds before testing
steps: On Friday night spend about 10 minutes writing what pass looks like
Go: at least 3 strangers take a real commitment step, ideally payment or pre-order
Fix: pain and engagement but no commitment; change only one of promise, price or buyer and rerun
Kill/park: no pain found and no one paying nearby
Write on a sticky note as your referee

quote.text: you're going to decide the pass mark before you start the test, not after.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Saturday research for existing spend and pain in buyer words
steps: Pick one buyer and one problem
Check Gumroad, Etsy, Teachable, Stan Store, Amazon for nearby products with reviews and sales counts
Mine Reddit, Facebook groups, forums, YouTube comments and 1-3 star competitor reviews
Copy exact phrases into a document without paraphrasing
Feed only the real quotes to ChatGPT to group by theme and rank pains
Target: 5+ real people describing the pain

quote.text: Copy the exact phrases that you find into a document. Don't paraphrase because you want their own words.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: One-paragraph offer plus mock-up landing page
steps: Answer who it is for, what result, exactly what they receive, and the price
Be concrete (e.g. 12-page checklist and three email templates)
Build a cover image, sample page or table of contents in 30-90 minutes
Put offer, mock-up and a buy/sign-up button on a simple landing page

quote.text: You don't need the product to test the product.
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Past-behaviour customer conversations
steps: Message 10-20 buyer-fit people, leading with a question not a pitch
Ask about the last time the problem happened, what they tried, what it cost
Show mock-up and price at the end and ask if they would want it this week
If yes, give them a way to act immediately

quote.text: Tell me about the last time this happened to you. What did you try? What did it cost you?
quote.speaker: Host

tactics.name: Honest pre-sale
steps: Include a real payment option on the landing page
State plainly it is a pre-sale with a specific ship date
Offer a full refund if you decide not to build
Fallback: specific waitlist, not a generic newsletter

quote.text: Payment is the strongest form of evidence you will ever get
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Evidence counts in proportion to what it costs the buyer: opinions are zero, existing spend, specific pain and commitment/payment climb the ladder.

quote.text: Evidence costs the buyers something. Time, attention, reputation, or money.

lessons.lesson: Speed of building with AI is not proof of demand; validate before building.

lessons.lesson: Pre-commit pass/fail thresholds so you cannot grade your own idea on a curve.
Narrow the buyer to a specific person, situation and cost rather than a crowd like 'busy people'.

quote.text: That's not a buyer, that's a crowd
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Competition signals an existing market; existing spend is good news.
Ask about past behaviour, not future promises.

quote.text: past behavior is evidence. Future promises, they're just compliments
quote.speaker: Host

lessons.lesson: Price, not free, tests real demand; pick a real price early.
Use AI for brainstorming, sorting and drafting but keep real customers as the source of truth.
Write down what evidence would prove you wrong to turn hope into a test.
A killed idea within 48 hours is a cheap win; change only one variable when fixing.

evidence_quality.rationale: Generic framework from a podcaster with only one first-hand data point (18 pre-sales for a course) and illustrative hypothetical numbers; the thresholds are self-described as not magic. Sound methodology but no verifiable results.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes the free weekend validation worksheet and the AI Escape Plan newsletter at darkhorseinsider.com.
